candidates.means_of_resistance: Explicit on-panel immunity: Shilo Norman explains that the painted symbol on his face is a New Gods alphabet letter meaning "freedom from restriction," and this lets him resist the Anti-Life Equation.
candidates.summary: Full resistance. Shilo Norman, as Mister Miracle, is shown explicitly resisting the Anti-Life Equation on-panel through a freedom symbol and explanation of how it works.
candidates.title: Mister Miracle (Shilo Norman)
candidates.what_visibly_happens: At Checkmate Castle, Shilo tells the others why he can resist the Equation, then the issue shows the wider battle continuing around him as the Anti-Life crisis unfolds.

candidates.title: Green Arrow (Oliver Queen)
candidates.what_visibly_happens: In the resistance pocket at the Hall of Justice, Green Arrow is among the heroes still active while Darkseid's forces overrun Earth.

candidates.means_of_resistance: Part of the remaining human resistance against Darkseid after the Anti-Life Equation has been broadcast worldwide; the source lists Oracle among the group still fighting back.

candidates.title: Oracle (Barbara Gordon)

candidates.means_of_resistance: Part of the remaining human resistance against Darkseid after the Anti-Life Equation has been broadcast worldwide; the source specifically names Joan Garrick with the resistance group.

candidates.title: Joan Garrick

content.notes: Conservative sweep of the retrieved sources only: included characters who are explicitly named as resisting, or who are directly described as able to resist, the Anti-Life Equation on-panel. Full resistance is only clearly supported for Mister Miracle/Shilo Norman. The others are partial/group resistance cases from the Hall of Justice resistance pocket; the retrieved snippets do not provide unique immunity mechanisms for them. I did not add characters that were merely discussed in commentary, fan replies, or adjacent Darkseid stories without explicit on-panel Anti-Life resistance evidence.

snippets:
"Darkseid Says": One month after the Anti-Life Equation was broadcast over every medium on Earth, the majority of humanity has fallen under the control of the Dark Gods. Ignorance reigns supreme, with only the Daily Planet left as a source of information. Final Crisis #4 is an issue of the series Final Crisis (Volume 1) with a cover date of November, 2008.
It's the Super Young Team, bearing Mister Miracle, who holds the key to defeating the Anti-Life Equation. However, he is shot by one of the pawns. In the Command-D Bunker, Turpin reaches the point of no return, when he must decide whether to continue struggling and die in agony, or give in and become Darkseid. Once the news of Mister Miracle's apparent demise reaches him, he decides there's really no choice at all. As the skies rain blood, the Dark God of Apokolips is reborn. ... This issue is reprinted in Final Crisis and Final Crisis New Edition.
The events from this issue take place after the events chronicled in Final Crisis: Submit #1. DC Comics solicitation reads: It's one month after the Anti-Life Equation was released worldwide. Millions now toil as slaves of Darkseid, while the Justifier shock troops of Apokolips lay waste to the planet Earth and hunt down its protectors.
One month after the Anti-Life Equation was broadcast over every medium on Earth, the majority of humanity has fallen under the control of the Dark Gods. Ignorance reigns supreme, with only the Daily Planet left as a source of information. Ray Terril arrives at the Hall of Justice, bringing with him Mark Richards, the Tattooed Man. It is there that he finds one of the few remaining pockets of resistance, consisting of Green Arrow, Black Canary, Oracle, the West family, and Joan Garrick.
